article_title: Git 2.56 Adds Safer Conflict Staging and Bulk Branch Cleanup, and Speeds Up Merge-Base Lookups on Large Repositories

content_preview.title: Git 2.56 Adds Safer Conflict Staging and Bulk Branch Cleanup, and Speeds Up Merge-Base Lookups on Large Repositories
content_preview.summary: Git 2.56.0 adds git add --resolved and git branch --delete-merged, plus a merge-base change that cut a Linux kernel lookup from 0.29 to 0.01 seconds.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Git project released Git 2.56.0 on September 28, 2026. According to [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1097213/), the release contains 748 non-merge commits made since Git 2.55 shipped in June, from 104 developers, 39 of them first-time contributors. New workflow commands include a safer way to stage resolved merge conflicts and a bulk command for deleting merged local branches, while a change to the merge-base search stopping rule accounts for the largest performance gains. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (826 words, within the 400-1200 range) with What Shipped, Other Additions and What We Don't Know sections. Technical detail is accurate and appropriately hedged (GitHub-reported benchmarks, no independent replication).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (gunzip, text-extracted). source-0.html.gz (GitHub Blog, Highlights from Git 2.56, Elijah Newren, Sept 28 2026): confirms verbatim/near-verbatim every claim attributed to it: git add --resolved considers only unmerged paths, scans unmerged regular files for conflict markers and leaves index unchanged, cannot combine with -u/-A, ignores never-conflicted tracked files; git branch --delete-merged with 'origin/*' and 'topic-*' patterns, --dry-run, skips worktree-checked-out branches, missing upstreams and ambiguous push configs, branch.<name>.deleteMerged=false; merge-base exclusive-painted-queue stopping rule, 0.68s to 0.01s monorepo case, ~70x and ~20x on two monorepos, Linux kernel git merge-base --all v4.8 v4.9 167,441 steps/0.29s to 3,887 steps/0.01s with default v2 commit-graph; path-walk repack with bitmaps and delta islands, Fluent UI 558.5 MB vs 164.4 MB (~71%), not default; Chromium ~500,000 index entries git diff eight minutes to 0.07s; 37,815 packs 4.5s O(N^2); git history drop (cannot operate on history with merge commits, cannot drop root/merge commit; reword/split in 2.54, fixup in 2.55); git refs create/update/delete/rename and rename reflog caveat; bisect run --reset-when-found; replay --linearize; git push origin/main suggestion; repack --filter=blob:limit=1m --drop-filtered, blob:limit only, GSoC by Siddharth Shrimali. source-1.html.gz (LWN, Git v2.56.0 released, quoting Junio Hamano's announcement of Mon 28 Sep 2026): confirms 748 non-merge commits since Git 2.55 in June, 104 developers, 39 first-time contributors. source-2.html.gz (Linuxiac): confirms the description of git add --resolved as staging files after conflict fixes while avoiding unrelated working-tree changes and checking for leftover conflict markers, plus delete-merged, refs, history drop, replay, and GitHub-reported merge-base gains. No snapshot failed; no WebFetch fallback used. All three manifests entries have suspicious_patterns: null, so no injection-scan matches to adjudicate.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace to the cited sources. One subordinate framing issue in the Overview: 'a change to the merge-base search stopping rule accounts for the largest performance gains' is not stated by any source. The GitHub Blog reports a larger single speedup elsewhere (a git diff on a Chromium checkout from about eight minutes to 0.07 seconds, and a 71% pack-size reduction from path-walk), and none of the three sources ranks the merge-base change as the largest. Not in headline or summary factual specifics; recoverable via a clarification.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; benchmark figures attributed to GitHub; no editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely distinct follow-up, not a duplicate. The published RC article (2026-09/22-git-256-release-candidate-...) centered on Rust becoming mandatory in Git 3.0 and the git refs toolbox, sourced from RelNotes/rc1 tags on github.com/git/git; it mentioned add --resolved, branch --delete-merged, bisect --reset-when-found and replay --linearize only as one-line release-note quotes. This article covers the final GA release (Sept 28), with new sources (GitHub Blog, LWN, Linuxiac), the actual mechanics and safeguards of the features, the benchmark data, path-walk repacking, history drop and release statistics, none of which the RC article covered, and it links back to the RC article. The submission was flagged as a follow-up (force-follow-up).
concerns: Overview lead states the merge-base change 'accounts for the largest performance gains', which no source supports; the GitHub Blog reports larger single-case gains elsewhere.
recommendations: Avoid ranking claims (largest, biggest) unless a cited source makes the comparison.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, distinct follow-up. One minor unsupported comparative claim in the Overview is covered by a single clarification; publish with corrections.
